subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens

question: After this branch is rebased, should OpenClaw preserve MCP/LSP runtime selector tokens in inherited spawned-child allowlists when those selectors pass the same effective policy layers as concrete tools?
rationale: This is an authorization-boundary behavior choice: preserving selectors fixes the documented subagent MCP loss, but maintainers must confirm the refreshed implementation cannot widen child access beyond the final policy intersection.

options.title: Refresh And Confirm Policy Parity
options.body: Resolve conflicts against current main and land only if the refreshed helper filters preserved selectors through profile, agent, group, subagent, inherited, runtime allow, and deny layers consistently with concrete tool filtering.

options.title: Replace At Runtime-Materialization Boundary
options.body: Pause this PR and replace it with an owner-authored fix closer to MCP/LSP materialization if preserving selectors in inherited session state is judged to be the wrong permanent boundary.

options.title: Accept After Manual Authorization Review
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the selector-preservation approach after conflict resolution if they judge the supplied proof and tests cover the child-session authorization boundary enough.

recommendation.title: Refresh And Confirm Policy Parity
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts against current main and land only if the refreshed helper filters preserved selectors through profile, agent, group, subagent, inherited, runtime allow, and deny layers consistently with concrete tool filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent declared allowlist work is the closest policy-filtering history that overlaps this PR's conflict and security-boundary question.
